description: A real QNN HTP v79 projection graph executed on the Hexagon DSP of a stock retail OnePlus 13 (CPH2655, SM8750, Android 16 SDK 36) from the TensorFold Android APK's untrusted_app context. Numerical output matched the ARM64 CPU oracle within the app-coded 0.0005 tolerance.
verdict: PASS for the fixed-synthetic HTP projection; DEFERRED for the two live-payload HTP projections (payload files not staged this session).

selinux_evidence.runas_app_evidence: run-as dev.tensorfold.mobile: stat /dev/fastrpc-cdsp -> Permission denied (from Stage 7B session attempt; runas_app context restricted vs untrusted_app)
selinux_evidence.untrusted_app_evidence: Direct open('/dev/fastrpc-cdsp') failed (Permission denied) AND fastrpc_apps_user.c:3844 open_shell failed; however the library fell back to the HAL path and cdsprpcd daemon (system UID) successfully opened /vendor/dsp/cdsp/fastrpc_shell_unsigned_3 on the app's behalf. Unsigned PD was then created on domain 3 (CDSP).

controls_and_distinctions.notes: The QnnProbe.cpp code path builds a real QNN HTP context, graph and MatMul node, executes QnnGraph_execute, reads back the output tensor, and compares to the integer CPU oracle. The 2.16 ms elapsed time is measured from the ARM side across the full QnnGraph_execute call which includes the FastRPC marshal to CDSP, the DSP-side kernel, and the result return.

tests_preserved.stage_7b_delta_this_session: No TensorFold source was modified in Stage 7B; only app binary install + run + UI capture + logcat + docs commit.

ties_back_to_stage_7a.stage_7a_finding: Shell-launched qnn-platform-validator reports 'Unit Test Passed' but strace shows EACCES on /dev/fastrpc-cdsp. The 'Pass' was ARM-side stub fallback, not HTP delegation.
ties_back_to_stage_7a.stage_7b_resolution: The TensorFold APK runs its QnnProbe JNI from the actual untrusted_app context which, unlike shell_UID or runas_app, has the Android loader-registered uses_native_library=libcdsprpc.so permission AND is permitted to reach cdsprpcd daemon via Binder/HAL. The daemon (system UID) opens the DSP shell on the app's behalf and returns a working PD handle. End result: the app can delegate to Hexagon v79; a shell binary of the same name cannot.
